en.title: New Killzone Game Reportedly in the Works — Remake or Remaster?
en.summary: Whispers suggest Sony is reviving the iconic PlayStation shooter franchise, Killzone, potentially with the help of People Can Fly. The big question remains whether fans will get a full remake or a remastered classic.
en.body:
After years of quiet, the **Killzone** franchise might be making a comeback. Reports indicate that Sony is exploring the revival of its once-flagship first-person shooter series, with **People Can Fly**, the studio behind **Bulletstorm** and **Outriders**, reportedly in talks to co-develop. This news surfaces as **Guerrilla Games**, the original creators of **Killzone**, has been fully immersed in the wildly successful **Horizon** universe since **Horizon Zero Dawn** launched in 2017. While **Guerrilla** has found immense success with Aloy's adventures, **Killzone** cultivated a dedicated fanbase who have long hoped for a return to the gritty intergalactic conflict.

The precise nature of this new **Killzone** project remains shrouded in mystery. Sources suggest it could be either a full remake or a remaster, breathing new life into one of the series' entries. Given its historical significance as the franchise's debut, the original **Killzone**, released on the PlayStation 2 in 2004, is a strong contender for such a treatment. Fans recall the original's ambitious scope and its role in establishing **PlayStation**'s shooter identity.

## A New Dawn for Helghast? ##

The **Killzone** series, once positioned as **Sony**'s answer to **Halo**, has been dormant since **Killzone Shadow Fall** accompanied the PlayStation 4's launch. While **Guerrilla Games** has publicly expressed a desire to move beyond the franchise, focusing on creating new IPs like **Horizon**, the enduring appeal of the Helghast and the ISA conflict hasn't faded for many players. The recent, albeit brief, crossover content in **Helldivers 2** also served as a potent reminder of **Killzone**'s visual identity and its place in **PlayStation** history. This potential revival could be **Sony**'s way of testing the waters for a full return to the series, perhaps paving the way for entirely new installments down the line.

## What's Next for the Franchise? ##

While details are still emerging, the involvement of **People Can Fly** suggests a focus on polished, action-packed gameplay, a hallmark of their previous titles. **Guerrilla Games** is currently juggling multiple projects, including the ongoing development of **Horizon** titles and the recent reboot of **Horizon Call of the Mountain**. If this **Killzone** project moves forward, it could be a significant undertaking, potentially aiming for a 2026 release. However, **Sony** has yet to make any official announcements, leaving fans to eagerly await confirmation.

content_raw: Sony is reportedly in the early stages of bringing its first-person shooter series, Killzone, back from the dead. Guerrilla Games’ Halo killer fell by the wayside after the developer found enormous success with Horizon Zero Dawn back in 2017. It has focused on the Horizon franchise ever since, but Killzone retains a loyal following, and fans often call for it to return. According to MP1st , Sony may be working on doing just that, with Bulletstorm and Outriders maker People Can Fly drafted in to co-dev. But what is this new Killzone game? Apparently it’s a Killzone remaster or remake, and while we’re not sure which Killzone is getting a fresh coat of paint, the first Killzone game, released on the PlayStation 2 in 2004, is a safe bet. There’s a lot going on at Guerrilla right now. PlayStation recently rebooted Horizon multiplayer spinoff Hunters Gathering following negative feedback , and, according to MP1st, the studio will move on to Killzone after it’s done doing that. According to Bloomberg , Guerrilla has until December to impress PlayStation bosses with Hunters Gathering’s next milestone, but already some Hunters Gathering staff moved over to another Guerrilla project with a milestone due at the end of this year. Apparently a “tiny team” is working on the next Horizon single-player game , which we’ll call Horizon 3 but will undoubtedly carry a new subtitle, but it’s still years away. Perhaps a Killzone remaster or remake is a way in for PlayStation to potentially reboot the series with a brand new game at some point down the line. Either way, it’s exciting news for Killzone fans, who haven’t heard a peep out of the franchise ever since PlayStation 4 launch title Killzone Shadow Fall ( save a T-shirt in The Last of Us Part 2: Remastered ) and a Helldivers 2 crossover . Speaking in 2024, Guerrilla Games art director Roy Postma declared the studio’s preference for the brighter, more vibrant world of Horizon over the dark and violent world of Killzone it had spent the previous decade working on. “We were done with it as a team,” Postma said . “As a studio, we needed to refresh the palette. It was, by choice, the opposite of Killzone.” Postma added that Horizon’s world has a wider appeal than Killzone’s: "I think the themes that this story and the characters represent are relatable for all ages and people, like having a found family of friends and finding your place in the world."
